video.acting_natural.evidence: [Riley·claude] Muted, the shot shows this: I (Riley, on the right) stand in the bathhouse entrance hall, say a word to the doorkeeper sitting on the left, and she looks up and holds out her hand. I take a handful of coins from my pocket and hold my palm out for her. She takes only one coin and puts it in her purse. I look down at what's left, smile, put the rest back, and keep smiling at her. Against the key point (she takes only the smallest coin and the ticket is surprisingly cheap), I read the beat through my own surprised look down and smile at 11.25–12.75s. Going through my beats one by one: 0–3.75s I stand about a metre from her with both hands hanging empty, head tilted slightly toward her, a small smile, looking at her face. My greeting falls in this stretch (I can't confirm the mouth at this thumbnail size, but my posture and gaze stay on her the whole time, so I'm not just standing there like a prop). 4.0s she holds out her hand. By 4.75s my left hand is in the left trouser pocket behind the cloth bag. 4.75–5.75s I'm digging in the pocket, about 1.5s, a natural length for finding money. 6.0s I look down at the coins in my hand. 6.25–6.5s I step forward and hold my palm above her hand. That's a reaction to her outstretched hand within about 2s, and the cause and effect are clear. 6.5–9.75s my arm stays out and my eyes stay on our hands and her fingers, so I'm watching her take the coin. 10.0–11.0s she turns to put the coin in her purse. My hand stays out with the remaining coins and I watch her, which is what I'd do: wait to see whether she wants more. 11.25–11.75s I look down at my palm and smile, a little unable to believe it. That's about 2s after she pinched the coin out at roughly 9s, but before that I was waiting to see if she'd take more, so it isn't a slow reaction. 12.0–12.75s I put the coins back in the pocket, still smiling as I look down. The smile is small, not bigger than the moment. 13.0–14.75s I look up at her and smile, my left hand still resting on the edge of the pocket at my hip. That's a natural pause after putting the money away, not a stiff posed hold. I don't reuse a gag, I don't make an overblown expression, and I don't make any move that's only there for the plot. Minor notes: in 13–14.75s the doorkeeper is still looking down at her purse, so my smile isn't met with eye contact, but she's the one who should look up. I can't make out my nod at this thumbnail size, and it doesn't affect the naturalness verdict.
